correctness.rationale: For even N, pairing k with k+N/2 and the parallelogram identity gives M^2 >= |c1|^2 + max|c0+c2 zeta^(2k)|^2. The N/2 roots have covering radius 2pi/N, giving the sharp two-term lower bound. Writing q=cos^2(pi/N) reduces it to M^2 >= |c1|^2+q(|c0|+|c2|)^2, and weighted Cauchy gives the stated upper bound. The displayed coefficient triple makes the paired terms pointwise orthogonal and attains every equality. No finite experiment is used to infer the infinite claim.

value.rationale: This is a sharp closed formula and extremizer for an infinite family of finite cyclic interpolation problems. It quantifies the exact sampling penalty relative to the classical continuous theorem and has a transparent geometric mechanism. The result is neither a routine parameter substitution nor a finite census; it isolates a natural invariant and its asymptotic bridge to the continuous case.
